title: List cancelled
stem:
You are an F2 doctor in orthopaedics. At 14:00 the afternoon theatre list is cancelled because an emergency case has taken the theatre. Four patients have been fasting since 07:00, and one has diabetes.

They are angry, and one says, "Nobody ever tells us anything."
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 5 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Ask the team to rebook their operations as soon as possible.
options.detailed: Knowing when their operations will happen helps reduce anxiety. It ranks third.

options.text: Avoid the bay until the nurses have told them.
options.detailed: This avoids a difficult conversation and may delay their eating and drinking. It is the least appropriate option.

options.text: Tell them it's the theatre team's fault.
options.detailed: The cancellation was due to an emergency. Blaming colleagues doesn't help.

options.text: Make sure they can eat and drink, and restart any medicines that were withheld.
options.brief: Prolonged fasting carries risks, especially in diabetes.
options.detailed: Patients, particularly those with diabetes, need to eat and restart medicines safely. It ranks second because it can happen straight after explaining.

options.text: Apologise, and explain why the list was cancelled and what's next.
options.brief: Honesty and an apology help reduce their frustration.
options.detailed: They deserve to know why their operations were cancelled and what will happen. An apology acknowledges their inconvenience. It ranks first.

explanation.issue: This tests how you respond to frustrated patients after a cancellation, combining honest communication with safety.
explanation.keyDetails: The list was cancelled for an emergency. Patients have fasted for seven hours. One has diabetes.
explanation.reasoning: [E] explains and apologises, [D] keeps them safe, and [A] plans ahead. [C] blames colleagues, and [B] avoids them.
explanation.competing: Some would make sure they can eat first. The key explains first because it takes a minute and it is what they need to hear.
